subdomain: 3.2 Analyze authentication and authorization requirements to identify security gaps

en.question: A public HTTP MCP client follows MCP 2026-07-28 authorization. Its selected OpenID Connect discovery document omits code_challenge_methods_supported. The identity team says TLS and exact redirect registration make the authorization-code exchange safe enough. What should the MCP client do under this specification?

options.text: Continue without PKCE because exact redirect registration authenticates the party redeeming the code.
options.note: Redirect validation does not replace proof that the redeemer holds the original PKCE verifier. This specification requires the client to verify PKCE support before authorization.

options.text: Send a plain code challenge and assume the provider supports it because the field is optional in OpenID Connect.
options.note: MCP adds an explicit requirement to verify this metadata field, even when using OpenID Connect discovery. Guessing support does not satisfy that requirement, and capable clients must use S256.

options.text: Complete authorization first and test whether the issued access token has an acceptable audience.
options.note: Audience validation protects resource access but does not repair an unprotected authorization-code flow. The missing PKCE capability must be addressed before proceeding.

options.text: Refuse to proceed until metadata verifies PKCE support, using S256 when technically capable.
options.note: MCP 2026-07-28 requires refusal when code_challenge_methods_supported is absent from either supported discovery mechanism. Its code-protection requirements are not waived by TLS or redirect checks.
